For in providing unverified & extraneous details that have no real bearing on the true matter at issue, you only succeed in supplying your opponents with something on which they can latch and use against you in an attempt to discredit your wider and more significant claims.

That is, if you push the narrative that he is just some 15 year old kid, and thereby either tacitly imply or outright assert that this aspect—the targeting of a minor—somehow makes CNN's behavior especially repulsive, then I fear you will in effect be unwittingly assisting CNN in damage control, in that so soon as this detail is later proven false (as it likely will be), your wider case will immediately suffer a two-fold blow: firstly, because errors in the details casts doubt about your overall credibility, and, secondly, because the accused's position now automatically upgrades to "not as bad" as you had first suggested.

[To further clarify this second point, what I mean is that if you immediately hit your opponent with all your most extravagant and dubious of claims, then their image can only improve from its transient initial low as these more tendentious of contentions are quickly shown unfounded or at least inadequately substantiated. In fact, insofar as many have an instinctive sympathy for the unjustly accused—even if the accused be an enemy—, in a mixture of slander and truth the former is apt to neutralize the latter and leave your opponent in even better standing than they had before.

[In short, then, throwing everything you have at your opponent and seeing what sticks is, at least in my mind, far less likely to bear fruit than a few incontestable and persistently pursued jabs. After all, it only takes one inconsistency—one discrepancy—to undermine eine Weltanschauung, and so it is better to continuously confront your opponents with some one fatal fact that they cannot deny, and which need must slowly eat away at their previous beliefs (caveat: this is only applicable to those of your opponents who are actually still capable of free thought; if their minds have become so ossified by disuse that reflection and thinking outside their routine thought patterns is no longer possible, then, needless to say, no amount of reason can suffice to save them), rather than to accuse them with something new and supposedly topical everyday, which, even if it be completely damning, ultimately has no lasting impact because long before it has had an opportunity to reach its full potential, attention has since been diverted many times over to the next and latest happenings. Yes, this means you will occasionally feel like an idiot, or at least a broken record, constantly reiterating the same things over again, but, for better or for worse, that is really the only way to reach the masses.
